The lesson shows how to connect before/after to actions using two sentence forms, how had plus a participle locates an earlier action, and how to rebuild order when an effect is mentioned first.
Filipino connector explanations distinguish time, overlap, cause, and result; worked examples demonstrate their use in a narrative and an informational report.
The text explicitly limits meanwhile and habang: overlap does not establish which action began first. Before need not mean immediately before.

Past perfect must be read with the later past event and surrounding text. Earlier events are not automatically causes, and a cause may continue during its effect. Reading Strategies tells students not to invent unstated order.

lesson-comprehension-skills-sequencing-o.quote: The order of the sentences is the **written order**. The order in which the events happened is the **event order**.
lesson-comprehension-skills-sequencing-o.note: The banned random-label table and its bare numerals are removed. The bridge passage wraps its numeral in inline math.

lesson-comprehension-skills-sequencing-o.quote: **Sequencing** means putting events in the order they happened. A passage may tell a later event first and explain an earlier event afterward.
lesson-comprehension-skills-sequencing-o.note: The opening now uses familiar words and explains the distinction directly without the former unexplained technical terms.
